title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. k is a base ring; the transcription's 'h' is the handwritten k. X_• is a simplicial set. S = k{T} is the divided-power polynomial algebra in one variable T. C^{··}_{DRpd}(X_•,k) is the bigraded S-algebra of divided-power polynomial de Rham forms on X_•. My understanding from the neighbouring pages is that these forms are homogenized: on the simplices one imposes Σ t_i = T instead of Σ t_i = 1, because with divided powers the relation Σ t_i = 1 cannot be imposed (γ_n(1) = 1/n! needs denominators). Setting T = 1 then recovers Sullivan's rational polynomial forms over k⊗Q (next page: C_DRS(X, k_Q) ≅ C_DRpd/(T−1)).

Previous page: computation of cohomology. In the bigrading (total degree n, exterior degree q) Grothendieck finds H'^{·,q}_{DRpd}(X,k) ≅ τ_q(H^q(X,k) ⊗_k k{T}), compatibly with products. Here τ_q is truncation to degrees ≥ q.

This page asks whether these 'shadows' τ_q(H^·⊗S) still carry all the information. He calls this the 'théorie des ombres' (theory of shadows).

1. Recovering a module. For a graded k-module M, with q large compared with the degrees of M, M is recovered up to canonical isomorphism from any one truncation τ_q(M⊗_k S). For n ≥ q + max deg M, the degree-n piece is ⊕_j M^j T^{[n−j]}. The exterior grading isolates each M^j, and multiplication by divided powers of T identifies the copies canonically.

2. Recovering a pairing. Pairings M⊗N→P are likewise recovered from the induced pairings τ_q(M_S)⊗τ_q(N_S)→τ_q(P_S). Grothendieck does not spell out why. The point is that the induced pairing on the components T^{[a]}, T^{[b]} is binom(a+b,a)·μ. Over arbitrary k these coefficients are not all invertible. But for a,b ≥ q the gcd of the binom(a+b,a) is 1 (Kummer: take a, b distinct powers of p, so there are no carries in base p). A Bézout combination therefore recovers μ itself.

3. Consequence. A graded k-algebra H^· concentrated in degrees ≥ 0 is determined by the bigraded S-algebra of its shadows. Hence the bigraded differential S-algebra C_DRpd(X,k) determines the cohomology ring H^·(X,k).

4. Hope. He further hopes ('voudrait que') that C_DRpd determines RΓ(X,k) in D(k) together with its cup product RΓ⊗^L RΓ → RΓ (continued on the next page). The next page then poses the integral analogue of Sullivan's theorem: for simply connected X_• of finite type, does C_DRpd with all its structure, including the divided powers, determine the homotopy type?
errors: The pairing-recovery step is stated without justification. Since T^{[a]}T^{[b]} = binom(a+b,a)T^{[a+b]}, one needs a gcd/Bézout argument over the binomial coefficients with a,b ≥ q. The argument works, but it is not written.
Recovering M needs boundedness hypotheses (q large relative to the degrees of M), which Grothendieck adds as an interlinear correction. For unbounded M one must argue degreewise.

The final hope (recovering RΓ with its derived cup product, or the homotopy type) is conjectural. Recovering the cohomology ring is far weaker than recovering the E∞/cochain-level structure. Nothing here establishes it.

ideas.what: Homogenized divided-power polynomial de Rham forms on simplicial sets: a bigraded k{T}-algebra whose reduction mod (T−1) gives Sullivan's rational forms (context from adjacent pages).
ideas.modern_name: integral / divided-power models of polynomial de Rham forms; Rees-type homogenization of Sullivan's A_PL
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (rational case, 1977); integral variants by Cenkl–Porter, Karoubi, and later binomial/E∞ approaches (Mandell, Toën, Horel, Kubrak–Shuklin–Zakharov)
ideas.where_published: Only the 1976 IHÉS talk, apparently unpublished; the schematization theme appears in Pursuing Stacks

ideas.what: 'Théorie des ombres': a graded module or algebra is recovered from any high truncation τ_q(M⊗k{T}) together with the induced pairings.
ideas.modern_name: no standard name; elementary reconstruction from truncated divided-power base change

ideas.what: Hope that the divided-power de Rham algebra determines RΓ(X,k) with its cup product, and (next page) the homotopy type of simply connected finite-type spaces.
ideas.modern_name: integral homotopy theory via cochain algebras; schematization problem
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mandell (E∞ cochains determine finite-type nilpotent spaces, 2001/2006); Toën (affine stacks, schematization); Ekedahl
ideas.where_published: Schematization of homotopy types is discussed in Pursuing Stacks (1983); not in this divided-power de Rham form

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes, around 1976, an integral strictly-commutative divided-power de Rham model of homotopy types. It is bigraded by a homogenizing variable T, recovers Sullivan's model after setting T=1, and is aimed at reconstructing integral cohomology rings and possibly homotopy types. This predates Mandell's E∞ theorem and the recent binomial-ring approaches, and is not cited in that literature.
missed.quote: Ce qui donne un espoir que le complexe de DR à p.d. de X_• ... donne l'information homotopique précise sur X_•
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Homogenized divided-power forms with a T-grading are a concrete candidate for integral models (cf. derived binomial rings, filtered/graded de Rham approaches). Comparing them with Horel's and Kubrak–Shuklin–Zakharov's binomial models could be fruitful.

missed.claim: The 'theory of shadows' (recovering H^· and its products from truncations τ_q(H⊗k{T})) is sketched. The hoped-for upgrade to recovering RΓ with its derived cup product from C_DRpd is left open.
missed.quote: Cette "théorie des ombres" étant supposée acquise ... on voudrait que ... RΓ(X_•,k) comme objet de la cat. dérivée D(k), l'accouplement
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Whether strictly commutative divided-power dg-algebras bigraded over k{T} capture integral cochain-level information, given the known obstructions from Steenrod operations, is a precise and unresolved-looking question for this particular construction.

deep.surprise_reason: The algebra on this page is elementary. The context is notable, though: an apparently unpublished 1976 Grothendieck programme for integral Sullivan-type models via homogenized divided-power forms, with an explicit homotopy-type question. It anticipates later work (Mandell, Toën, binomial rings) and does not seem to be recorded in the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'h-module', 'M⊗_h S', 'h-algèbre', 'C(X_•,h)', 'H^·(X_•,h)', 'RΓ(X_•,h)', 'D(h)' should all read k (the base ring), not h.
'𝔛_x' / '𝒳_x' denotes the simplicial set X_• (subscript bullet, not x).
'(comme dans le cas h=Q)' should read 'k=ℚ'.
Interlinear insertion after τ_q(M⊗_k S): roughly 'pourvu que q grand devant les degrés de M' (q large relative to the degrees of M).
'dans les composantes de degré ("extérieur") ≤ q' refers to exterior-degree components of the bigraded S-algebra.
The insertion before 'acquise' reads 'supposée' (the theory of shadows being assumed acquired).
